why: A = theorem_6_6_11 ∧ push_eq_of_homotopy (universes at 0). B = (B1) every smooth x of a tame X has an open, sc-smoothly contractible U ∋ x with HasLocalPropagation in some chart, for any sc-Fredholm f, ∧ (B2) two sc-smooth paths with the same end points in an open sc-smoothly contractible U are sc-smoothly homotopic in U rel end points. B ⇒ theorem_6_6_11 is proved (B_to_theorem_6_35: B1 has weaker hypotheses and a stronger conclusion), but B ⇒ push_eq_of_homotopy is not: that lemma is about an arbitrary homotopy in the domain of an arbitrary chart (with a section as in Prop. 6.28 (3)), while B only gives the propagation property on some neighbourhood of each point; getting it would mean re-proving the analytic homotopy argument (Lemma 6.29 on the square, push_square) or a covering/chart-change argument. A ⇒ B fails for three genuine reasons: (i) contractibility — theorem_6_35's U comes from Proposition 6.28 with property (1′) (paths in U are homotopic in a larger W ⊆ dom c), and is not shown to be sc-smoothly contractible; the project replaces 'contractible U' by the pair U ⊆ W; (ii) A's hypotheses PX.AdmitsBumpFunctions, B.IsScFredholmSectionTame f (tame germ data at every smooth point) and the families ParacompactSpace ((Fin k → ℝ) × ((Fin n → ℝ) × X)), ParacompactSpace (pullbackSpace (pullbackProj P snd) snd) are not given by B (all satisfiable: admitsBumpFunctions_of_hilbert, whole-chart tame sections, metrizable X); (iii) B2 is a statement of path topology (contractible ⇒ simply connected rel end points, inside U) with no counterpart in A, which never needs it. B2 is believed true but is a substantial sc-smooth square-lemma construction; B1 without bump functions is the blind author's DOUBT (push-forwards need sc⁺-sections) and may fail for bundles without sc⁺-sections.
